newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shareholders approve CEPA privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Shareholders approve CEPA privatisation.

text.p: Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA) said on Monday its shareholders and those of Hopewell Holdings Ltd have approved the privatisation scheme as offered by Southern Co of the United States.

Hopewell shareholders voted unanimously in favour of the scheme while CEPA shareholders voted overwhelmingly in favour of a deal at separate extraordinary general meetings on Monday, CEPA and Hopewell spokesmen told reporters after the meetings.
The deal will privatise CEPA but ensure that Hopewell maintains a minority stake of between 12.1 and 20 percent, down from the 60.4 percent it now holds.

Hopewell will receive between HK$9.64 billion and HK$12.26 billion in cash from Southern, depending on which of two offers CEPA shareholders elect to take, said Lawrence Miao, executive director of CEPA.
Southern has proposed two options to CEPA shareholders.

The first option is a straightforward offer of HK$18.50 per CEPA share. The second option offers shareholders one new CEPA share, cash of HK$69.50 and a "contingency entitlement" of HK$8.00 for every five CEPA shares held.
The contingency payment depends on the achievement of limited recourse debt for a power plant project in Indonesia and a final dividend of HK$0.15 per share.
CEPA said it was still in discussions relating to a project financing package funding the Tanjung Jati B Plant in Indonesia which will satisfy the payment condition for the contingency entitlement.

Hopewell executive director Robert Nien said the company was studying its debt repayment schedule but would not say how much of the funds received from the sale of Hopewell's CEPA shares would be applied to debt and how much to working capital.
Hopewell chairman Gordon Wu said in October that Hopewell's gearing was 92 percent and would fall to as low as 23 percent as a result of the deal.
